## Q1
Which document outlines the functional and non-functional requirements of a software system?

## Q1 - Options
(A) SRS document
(B) Design document
(C) Test plan
(D) User manual

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q10

A Software Requirements Specification defines what the system must do and the quality constraints it must meet. Design documents describe implementation choices, while test plans and manuals serve later purposes.

## Q4
Match List-I (Process/lifecycle models) with List-II.

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| A. V-Model | I. Trigger transition |
| B. Incremental process model | II. Classic life cycle |
| C. Spiral Model | III. Risk Driven |
| D. Concurrent Model | IV. Core product |

## Q4 - Options
(A) A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II
(B) A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
(C) A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
(D) A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

## Q4 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q11

Each process model is best known for one specific descriptive tag from the software engineering literature.

A-II — The V-Model is a variant of the classic waterfall life cycle that pairs each development stage with a corresponding testing stage.

B-IV — The incremental model delivers a core product in the first increment, then adds features in successive increments.

C-III — The spiral model is explicitly risk-driven, since each loop of the spiral begins with a risk analysis before proceeding.

D-I — The concurrent development model represents each software element as being in one of several states, moving between them through triggered event transitions.

A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I is therefore the correct match.

## Q5
Which is not a requirements-elicitation technique?

## Q5 - Options
(A) Interviews
(B) The use-case approach
(C) Facilitated Application Specification Technique (FAST)
(D) Data-flow diagram

## Q5 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2025 (26 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q22

Interviews, use cases, and FAST are techniques for discovering and negotiating requirements. A data-flow diagram models how data moves through a system; it may document requirements but is not itself an elicitation technique.

## Q6
Which is not a software characteristic?

## Q6 - Options
(A) Software does not wear out.
(B) Software is flexible.
(C) Software is not manufactured.
(D) Software is always correct.

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2025 (26 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q25

Software can contain defects, so it is not always correct. Unlike physical hardware it does not wear out through use, it can be changed, and it is developed rather than manufactured in the usual physical sense.

## Q12
Arrange the following steps of Feature Drive<br>
Development (FDD) process in the correct sequence :<br>
A. Develop an overall model<br>
B. Build by feature<br>
C. Plan by feature<br>
D. Design by feature<br>
E. Build a feature list

## Q12 - Options
(A) (A), (C), (B), (E), (D)
(B) (A), (E), (C), (D), (B)
(C) (B),(A),(D),(E),(C)

## Q12 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Aug 2024 (23 Aug, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q10

## Q19
Assertion (A): Validity checks real need of system users.<br>
Reason (R): Completeness checks system user defined requirements.

## Q19 - Options
(A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
(B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
(C) A is true but R is false
(D) A is false but R is true

## Q19 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q33

In requirements validation, validity and completeness are two separate checks with distinct purposes.

Validity checks whether the system provides the functions that best support the customer's real needs, so Assertion A is true.

Completeness checks whether the requirements document includes all the functions the customer actually requires, so Reason R is also a true statement on its own.

However, R describes a different check, completeness, from the one Assertion A is about, validity. Completeness does not explain why validity checks real need — the two are parallel, independent quality checks on a requirements document, not cause and effect. So both statements are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

## Q20
An observational technique that can be used to understand operational process and help to derive requirement for software to support operational process is known as

## Q20 - Options
(A) Requirement specification
(B) Structural specification
(C) Ethnography
(D) Natural language specification

## Q20 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** SDLC Models & Requirements (SRS)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q63

Ethnography is a requirements engineering technique borrowed from social science, where an observer studies people performing their actual work in context to uncover the real operational process, including informal practices that formal interviews or documents miss. This directly matches an observational technique used to understand an operational process and derive requirements from it.

- **A. Requirement specification** — the document that records requirements, not the observational technique used to discover them.
- **B. Structural specification** — not a standard requirements-engineering observational technique.
- **C. Ethnography** — correct. It is the standard named observational technique for studying operational work practice.
- **D. Natural language specification** — a way of writing requirements in prose, not an observational technique.
